$comment: NON-NORMATIVE. This vocabulary is a conformance-suite diagnostic aid, not part of the CDX specification. The specification mandates DISPOSITIONS (State Machine section 5.4) and lineage OUTCOMES (Provenance and Lineage section 3.3) — never error identifiers. A conforming implementation is free to use its own internal errors and map them to these codes in its conformance adapter; it is never required to adopt this vocabulary. A code sharpens a failure report and is never by itself the pass criterion for a MUST — the normative assertion is the `disposition` each entry records.

compatibilityPolicy.summary: Codes are append-only and permanently stable once published.
rules: A code is NEVER re-pointed at a different defect. If the meaning must change, a new code is added and the old one is deprecated.
A deprecated code keeps its entry forever, gaining `deprecated: true` and, where applicable, `supersededBy`. Entries are never deleted.
`version` is the vocabulary's own semantic version and bumps on any addition or deprecation.
`specVersion` is the CDX specification version the `clause` citations resolve against.

dispositionNote: `disposition` records the load-time disposition the SPECIFICATION assigns to this defect class (State Machine section 5.4), with `dispositionClause` naming the row relied on. It is the normative half of an entry. A null disposition means the specification assigns no document-level disposition to this defect — not that a consumer may ignore it. NOTE for STATE-VARYING rows: a few section 5.4.2 rows assign different dispositions by document state (e.g. a structurally malformed block/mark of a known type is WARNING in draft/review but INTEGRITY-ERROR in frozen/published). The scalar `disposition` records the state-invariant or draft/review disposition; any frozen/published escalation is described in `note` pending a state-aware model. This is a widening of an entry's stated disposition for higher-integrity states, not a re-pointing of the code to a different defect, so it is compatible with the append-only policy. NOTE for lineage entries: the lineage OUTCOME vocabulary (VERIFIED/INCOMPLETE/REJECTED, Provenance and Lineage section 3.3) is a different axis from the DISPOSITION vocabulary (IGNORE/WARNING/INTEGRITY-ERROR/REJECT). A lineage outcome of REJECTED does NOT mean the disposition REJECT: a proven-forged lineage is a WARNING, because the document's content identity is unaffected and it is not blocked on lineage grounds.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-ID-PENDING.summary: A manifest projection was requested for a document whose id is still `pending`.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-ID-PENDING.dispositionClause: Not a document defect: the manifest is well-formed and the projection is simply undefined until the document id is assigned. No load-time disposition applies.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-ID-PENDING.note: The projection is defined only once the document id is fixed.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-HASH-MALFORMED.summary: A declared content hash is absent, or is not a well-formed `algorithm:hexdigest`.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-HASH-MALFORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (manifest absent, unparseable, or missing or mistyping a required field)

CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-MALFORMED.summary: A declared file reference is not a well-formed `{path, hash}` object (not an object, or a missing/non-string path).
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-MALFORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (manifest absent, unparseable, or missing or mistyping a required field)
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-MALFORMED.note: Distinct from CDX-E-MANIFEST-HASH-MALFORMED: the defect is the shape of the reference, not the hash value. ALSO emitted for a MISTYPED `metadata` object or `metadata.dublinCore` path: both are required manifest fields (Manifest section 4.7), so a present-but-wrong-typed one is State Machine section 5.4.2's "manifest ... missing or mistyping a required field" REJECT. That reference is a bare relative-path string rather than a `{path, hash}` object, so the summary's shape does not describe it; the defect CLASS is the same — a manifest reference that cannot be interpreted — which is why this code is reused rather than a new one minted, the append-only policy forbidding a code from being re-pointed but not from covering a further instance of its own class.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-PATH-TRAVERSAL.summary: A declared path is not a safe archive-relative path (escapes the archive root).
CDX-E-MANIFEST-PATH-TRAVERSAL.clause: Security Extension section 9.7; Container Format section 9.1
CDX-E-MANIFEST-PATH-TRAVERSAL.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (an unsafe archive path or symlink always REJECTs, in every state)

CDX-E-MANIFEST-VERSION-MALFORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (manifest absent, unparseable, or missing or mistyping a required field)

CDX-E-MANIFEST-STATE-UNKNOWN.clause: State Machine section 3.1; Security Extension section 9.7
CDX-E-MANIFEST-STATE-UNKNOWN.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (a `state` value outside the defined lifecycle enum, so the mutability-and-signature contract cannot be established)

CDX-E-MANIFEST-EXTENSION-DUPLICATE.summary: Two `manifest.extensions[]` entries share an id, making the projection ambiguous.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-EXTENSION-DUPLICATE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns NO row to this defect class. The projection fails closed on it (the projected bytes would otherwise be ambiguous), but the specification does not state a load-time disposition and none is inferred here — notably the generic "missing or mistyping a required field" row does not reach it, since section 5.4.2 gives the `state` enum its own dedicated row rather than relying on that one. Tracked as a specification gap.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-PRESENTATION-TYPE-UNKNOWN.summary: A `manifest.presentation[]` entry declares a type outside the enum.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-PRESENTATION-TYPE-UNKNOWN.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns NO row to this defect class. The projection fails closed on it (the projected bytes would otherwise be ambiguous), but the specification does not state a load-time disposition and none is inferred here — notably the generic "missing or mistyping a required field" row does not reach it, since section 5.4.2 gives the `state` enum its own dedicated row rather than relying on that one. Tracked as a specification gap.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-HASH-CONFLICT.summary: The same declared path appears twice with conflicting hashes.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-HASH-CONFLICT.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns NO row to this defect class. The projection fails closed on it (the projected bytes would otherwise be ambiguous), but the specification does not state a load-time disposition and none is inferred here — notably the generic "missing or mistyping a required field" row does not reach it, since section 5.4.2 gives the `state` enum its own dedicated row rather than relying on that one. Tracked as a specification gap.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-HASH-CONFLICT.note: Emitted for the config-file references and the asset-index references.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-REQUIRED-SIGNER-SET-INVAL.summary: `signaturePolicy.requiredSigners` is absent, is not an array, or is empty.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REQUIRED-SIGNER-SET-INVAL.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns NO row to this defect class. The projection fails closed on it (the projected bytes would otherwise be ambiguous), but the specification does not state a load-time disposition and none is inferred here — notably the generic "missing or mistyping a required field" row does not reach it, since section 5.4.2 gives the `state` enum its own dedicated row rather than relying on that one. Tracked as a specification gap.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REQUIRED-SIGNER-SET-INVAL.note: An empty set is forbidden so an absent policy and an empty policy are not both expressible.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-REQUIRED-SIGNER-DUPLICATE.summary: Two `requiredSigners` entries declare the same identity.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REQUIRED-SIGNER-DUPLICATE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns NO row to this defect class. The projection fails closed on it (the projected bytes would otherwise be ambiguous), but the specification does not state a load-time disposition and none is inferred here — notably the generic "missing or mistyping a required field" row does not reach it, since section 5.4.2 gives the `state` enum its own dedicated row rather than relying on that one. Tracked as a specification gap.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-REQUIRED-SIGNER-KIND-AMBI.summary: A `requiredSigners` entry carries zero, or more than one, identity kind.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REQUIRED-SIGNER-KIND-AMBI.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns NO row to this defect class. The projection fails closed on it (the projected bytes would otherwise be ambiguous), but the specification does not state a load-time disposition and none is inferred here — notably the generic "missing or mistyping a required field" row does not reach it, since section 5.4.2 gives the `state` enum its own dedicated row rather than relying on that one. Tracked as a specification gap.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REQUIRED-SIGNER-KIND-AMBI.note: Spans both the zero-kind and multiple-kind cases: section 3.12 requires exactly one identity kind, and this implementation fails closed on either violation at a single guard.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-REQUIRED-SIGNER-ID-MALFOR.summary: A `requiredSigners` identity value is malformed for its declared kind.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-REQUIRED-SIGNER-ID-MALFOR.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 assigns NO row to this defect class. The projection fails closed on it (the projected bytes would otherwise be ambiguous), but the specification does not state a load-time disposition and none is inferred here — notably the generic "missing or mistyping a required field" row does not reach it, since section 5.4.2 gives the `state` enum its own dedicated row rather than relying on that one. Tracked as a specification gap.

CDX-E-MANIFEST-ABSENT.summary: The archive contains no `manifest.json` entry, so the document has no manifest to load.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-ABSENT.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (manifest absent, unparseable, or missing or mistyping a required field)

CDX-E-MANIFEST-UNPARSEABLE.summary: `manifest.json` is present but is not well-formed JSON (a bare syntax error), or is valid JSON that is not an object, so it cannot be parsed as a manifest.
CDX-E-MANIFEST-UNPARSEABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (manifest absent, unparseable, or missing or mistyping a required field)
CDX-E-MANIFEST-UNPARSEABLE.note: Distinct from CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS, which is a canonical-JSON violation detected structurally rather than a JSON syntax error, and from CDX-E-MANIFEST-*-MALFORMED, which fire on a parseable manifest OBJECT with a bad field.

CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS.summary: A JSON part contains an object with duplicate keys, which the canonical-JSON rules forbid before any hashing or verification.
CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (duplicate JSON keys in any part always REJECT, in every state)
CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS.note: An unrejected duplicate key permits a split-view substitution — one key-value pair is hashed while a colliding one is materialized — so the rejection is state-invariant, exactly like a duplicate archive entry.

CDX-E-PART-NUMBER-NON-REPRESENTABLE.summary: A hashed JSON number is non-finite, or an integer whose magnitude exceeds 2^53 - 1, so the IEEE-754 double the canonicalizer hashes would differ from the value the author wrote.
CDX-E-PART-NUMBER-NON-REPRESENTABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (a non-representable hashed number always REJECTs, in every state)

CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-MISSING.summary: The required content part is absent: `manifest.content.path` is a valid archive-relative path but names no existing archive entry.
CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-MISSING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (missing the required content part)
CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-MISSING.note: A missing or non-string content reference is caught earlier as CDX-E-MANIFEST-REFERENCE-MALFORMED; this code fires only when the reference is well-formed but no entry backs the path. An encrypted content part mapped to a stored `.enc` entry by the security extension satisfies the presence requirement (State Machine section 5.4.2 note 5).

CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-UNPARSEABLE.summary: The content part is present but cannot be parsed as JSON — a bare syntax error, or a decompression / parser-resource-limit failure — so the content and the document's identity cannot be established.
CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-UNPARSEABLE.clause: Document Hashing section 4.3.2; State Machine section 5.4.1
CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-UNPARSEABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.1 (a document that cannot be parsed, or whose identity cannot be established, is a REJECT): the content part is required canonical JSON (Document Hashing section 4.3.2), so a content part that cannot be parsed yields no canonical content in any state — and, once an id is assigned, makes its recomputation impossible.
CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-UNPARSEABLE.note: Distinct from CDX-E-CONTENT-PART-MISSING (no entry backs the path) and CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS (a canonical-JSON structural violation with its own code). Scoped to the required content part; a missing or unparseable NON-content part (Dublin Core, presentation) is a separate later-phase disposition.

CDX-E-VERSION-MAJOR-UNSUPPORTED.summary: The manifest `cdx` field declares a major format version this reader does not implement, so the document cannot be safely interpreted.

CDX-E-VERSION-MINOR-UNSUPPORTED.summary: The manifest `cdx` field declares a minor format version newer than this reader implements; known fields are processed and unknown additions ignored.
CDX-E-VERSION-MINOR-UNSUPPORTED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unsupported minor version — process known fields, IGNORE unknown additions)

CDX-E-EXTENSION-REQUIRED-UNSUPPORTED.summary: A manifest extension marked `required: true` names a namespace this reader does not support, so the document cannot be fully interpreted.
CDX-E-EXTENSION-REQUIRED-UNSUPPORTED.note: An encrypted document declares cdx.security as required:true, so a reader without security-extension support rejects it through this row rather than misreading the archive (State Machine section 5.4.2 note 5).

CDX-E-EXTENSION-OPTIONAL-UNSUPPORTED.summary: A manifest extension marked `required: false` names a namespace this reader does not support; its data is skipped and the document degrades gracefully.
CDX-E-EXTENSION-OPTIONAL-UNSUPPORTED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unsupported optional extension — degrade; SHOULD surface)

CDX-E-LINEAGE-CYCLE.summary: The lineage walk revisited a document already on the current path.
CDX-E-LINEAGE-CYCLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (REJECTED lineage — WARNING in every state)
CDX-E-LINEAGE-CYCLE.note: The lineage MUST be treated as forged — a verifier MUST NOT present any claimed ancestry as authenticated, and MUST surface the proven inconsistency as distinct from a merely unverifiable chain. The document's content identity is unaffected, so it is NOT blocked on lineage grounds: the outcome REJECTED is not the disposition REJECT.

CDX-E-LINEAGE-ANCESTORS-CONTRADICT.summary: A declared `ancestors` entry contradicts the resolved parent chain (forged tail).
CDX-E-LINEAGE-ANCESTORS-CONTRADICT.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (REJECTED lineage — WARNING in every state)
CDX-E-LINEAGE-ANCESTORS-CONTRADICT.note: Forged lineage: claimed ancestry MUST NOT be presented as authenticated, but the document is not blocked on lineage grounds. The outcome REJECTED is not the disposition REJECT.

CDX-E-LINEAGE-ROOT-WITH-ANCESTORS.summary: A document declaring no parent also declares a non-empty ancestors chain.
CDX-E-LINEAGE-ROOT-WITH-ANCESTORS.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (REJECTED lineage — WARNING in every state)
CDX-E-LINEAGE-ROOT-WITH-ANCESTORS.note: Forged lineage: claimed ancestry MUST NOT be presented as authenticated, but the document is not blocked on lineage grounds. The outcome REJECTED is not the disposition REJECT.

CDX-E-LINEAGE-UNRESOLVABLE.summary: A link in the chain could not be resolved, so the chain cannot be fully walked.
CDX-E-LINEAGE-UNRESOLVABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (INCOMPLETE lineage — WARNING in every state)
CDX-E-LINEAGE-UNRESOLVABLE.note: Unverified, never endorsed: no ancestor beyond the break is presented as verified. An unverifiable proof never rejects the document (section 5.4.3).

CDX-E-LINEAGE-BOUND-REACHED.summary: The traversal depth or breadth bound was reached before the walk completed.
CDX-E-LINEAGE-BOUND-REACHED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (INCOMPLETE lineage — WARNING in every state)
CDX-E-LINEAGE-BOUND-REACHED.note: A legitimately deep or wide history is not an inconsistency.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-UNREADABLE.summary: The archive cannot be parsed as a ZIP: no End Of Central Directory record, or a truncated or malformed central directory.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-UNREADABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Archive unreadable ... REJECT in every state)

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DUPLICATE-ENTRY.summary: Two central-directory entries resolve to the same path after the section 3.4 normalization.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DUPLICATE-ENTRY.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (Duplicate archive entries always REJECT, in every state)
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DUPLICATE-ENTRY.note: Closes a split-view substitution: a signer's tooling hashes one entry into the document id while a victim's reader materializes a different entry of the same name under one still-valid signature.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-CASE-COLLISION.summary: Two central-directory entries differ only in case, colliding when extracted onto a case-insensitive filesystem.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-CASE-COLLISION.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (Duplicate archive entries, including a case-only collision, always REJECT, in every state)

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-LFH-CD-DISAGREEMENT.summary: The local-file-header view and the central-directory view disagree on the entry set: a central entry with no matching local header, or a local name that differs from its central name.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-LFH-CD-DISAGREEMENT.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (local-file-header/central-directory entry-set disagreement always REJECTs, in every state)

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DATA-OUTSIDE-CD.summary: A local file header exists that the central directory does not enumerate (file data outside the authoritative index).
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DATA-OUTSIDE-CD.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (local-file-header/central-directory entry-set disagreement always REJECTs, in every state)
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DATA-OUTSIDE-CD.note: The central directory is the authoritative index; a stray local entry is a split-view substitution vector.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-UNSAFE-NAME.summary: An archive entry name fails the section 9.1 safety checks: a `..` segment, an absolute or drive/UNC/colon-bearing name, a backslash, a reserved Windows device name, a trailing dot/space segment, or an overlong or ill-formed UTF-8 encoding.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-UNSAFE-NAME.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (an unsafe archive path or symlink always REJECTs, in every state)

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-SYMLINK-ENTRY.summary: An archive entry encodes a symbolic link (a Unix mode with the symlink bit set).
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-SYMLINK-ENTRY.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.3 (an unsafe archive path or symlink always REJECTs, in every state)
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-SYMLINK-ENTRY.note: CDX defines no legitimate use for a symlink entry; it is a second path-traversal vector.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DECOMPRESSION-BOMB.summary: A declared entry size, decompression ratio, or archive total exceeds the reader's finite bound.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DECOMPRESSION-BOMB.dispositionClause: Container Format sections 5.3 and 9.2 (a conforming reader MUST enforce a finite bound on every attacker-controlled dimension and MUST fail closed -- reject the archive -- when one is exceeded). Section 5.4.2 does not itself enumerate this class; the disposition is stated in the mechanism sections.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-DECOMPRESSION-BOMB.note: The specific thresholds are implementation-defined (section 5.1 gives reasonable defaults); the existence and enforcement of a bound is the requirement. A fixture bomb must exceed any plausible conformant bound, not one specific threshold.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-CRC-MISMATCH.summary: A stored ZIP CRC-32 does not match the CRC recomputed over the entry's actual bytes (a corrupt entry).
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-CRC-MISMATCH.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (ZIP CRC-32 mismatch for an archive entry). The stored bytes cannot be trusted to decompress to the content they claim, independently of the semantic document hash (section 6.2).

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-FIRST-FILE-NOT-MANIFEST.summary: The first archive entry is not `manifest.json`.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-FIRST-FILE-NOT-MANIFEST.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (the first archive entry is not manifest.json). The archive is fully readable and the manifest resolvable by name, so only the streaming/quick-validation optimization is lost.

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENCRYPTION-USED.summary: An entry uses ZIP-level encryption (general-purpose bit 0 set); CDX uses the security extension for encryption, never the container.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-ENCRYPTION-USED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (ZIP-level encryption present, or a multi-volume archive, both forbidden by Container Format section 3.1 and neither coherently loadable)

CDX-E-ARCHIVE-MULTI-VOLUME.summary: The archive is a multi-volume (split) ZIP: an End Of Central Directory disk field is non-zero.
CDX-E-ARCHIVE-MULTI-VOLUME.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (ZIP-level encryption present, or a multi-volume archive, both forbidden by Container Format section 3.1 and neither coherently loadable)

CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.summary: A content block has an unrecognized but well-formed namespaced type (`ns:name`, e.g. `myorg:widget`) — an extension block type this reader does not implement.
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.clause: Content Blocks section 5; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unknown namespaced block or mark type — IGNORE, render a fallback). State-invariant.
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.note: "Namespaced" is the schema's extension-type form (a non-empty prefix, a colon, a non-empty suffix); a registered namespaced type such as academic:theorem is in the known set and is NOT reported here (Content Blocks section 5.1 line 1019).

CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.summary: A content block has an unrecognized type that is not a well-formed namespaced identifier: a bare or misspelled type (e.g. `paragrph`), a colon-malformed type (`:x`, `x:`), a missing or non-string `type`, or a non-object in a block position — none of which can be deferred to an extension fallback.
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.clause: Content Blocks section 5; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unknown bare, non-namespaced block or mark type — REJECT). State-invariant; Content Blocks section 5.1 line 1017 frames the bare-vs-namespaced split so a misspelled core type is caught rather than silently accepted.
CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.note: Fail-closed: only a well-formed namespaced identifier earns the lenient IGNORE of CDX-E-BLOCK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED; every other unrecognized block type is bare and REJECTs.

CDX-E-BLOCK-MALFORMED.summary: A block of a KNOWN CORE type violates a structural constraint JSON Schema cannot express: upward containment (e.g. a `tableCell`, `tableRow`, or `figcaption` outside its required parent), figure / definitionItem cardinality, or a node-bearing field of the wrong shape — on the block or on one of its subfigures — (`children`/`subfigures`/`marks` present but not an array, `caption` present but neither array nor string, or a `subfigures` element that is not an object).
CDX-E-BLOCK-MALFORMED.clause: Content Blocks section 7.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-BLOCK-MALFORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (structurally malformed block or mark of a known type — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-BLOCK-MALFORMED.note: This code carries the DRAFT/REVIEW disposition only. The FROZEN/PUBLISHED escalation to INTEGRITY-ERROR is gated on a valid signature (State Machine section 5.3) and is deferred to B3; every B1b-2 fixture is a draft.

CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.summary: A text-node mark has an unrecognized but well-formed namespaced type (`ns:name`, e.g. `myorg:flag`), in either bare-string or typed-object form — an extension mark this reader does not implement.
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.clause: Content Blocks section 5.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unknown namespaced block or mark type — IGNORE, render the unmarked text). State-invariant.
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED.note: A registered namespaced mark such as legal:cite is in the known set and is NOT reported here (Content Blocks section 5.1 line 1019).

CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.summary: A text-node mark has an unrecognized type that is not a well-formed namespaced identifier: a bare or misspelled mark string (e.g. `itlaic`), a colon-malformed mark, a mark object with a missing or non-string `type`, or a mark that is neither a string nor an object.
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.clause: Content Blocks section 5.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (unknown bare, non-namespaced block or mark type — REJECT). State-invariant; Content Blocks section 5.1 line 1017: an unrecognized bare mark is rejected as malformed, so a misspelled core mark is not silently accepted as an unknown mark.
CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-BARE.note: Fail-closed: only a well-formed namespaced identifier earns the lenient IGNORE of CDX-E-MARK-TYPE-UNKNOWN-NAMESPACED; every other unrecognized mark type is bare and REJECTs.

CDX-E-MARK-MALFORMED.summary: A mark of a KNOWN type is structurally malformed for that type: a core structured mark missing a required field (`link` without `href`, `anchor` without `id`, `math` without `format`/`source`), a core string mark (bold, italic, …) carried as an object, or a structured mark used as a bare string.
CDX-E-MARK-MALFORMED.clause: Content Blocks section 5.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-MARK-MALFORMED.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (structurally malformed block or mark of a known type — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-MARK-MALFORMED.note: This code carries the DRAFT/REVIEW disposition only; the FROZEN/PUBLISHED INTEGRITY-ERROR escalation is deferred to B3 (State Machine section 5.3). The internal field validation of the registered EXTENSION structured marks (citation, footnote, entity, glossary, academic:*-ref, presentation:*, legal:cite) is deferred; those types are in the known set, so they are neither rejected nor ignored.

CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.summary: A declared file-level hash does not match the exact stored bytes it pins: the digest of the content part's raw decompressed bytes, under the algorithm named by the hash's own prefix (Document Hashing section 3.3), differs from `manifest.content.hash`.
CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.clause: Document Hashing sections 5.1, 6.3; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (File `hash` or document-ID mismatch — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH.note: STATE-VARYING: the DRAFT/REVIEW disposition is WARNING; on a FROZEN/PUBLISHED document it escalates to INTEGRITY-ERROR (state-keyed per Document Hashing section 6.3 — the document asserts fixed, integrity-checked bytes). The escalation is deferred to B3: soundly trusting `state = frozen`/`published` requires a projection-covering signature (State Machine section 5.4.2 note 3, lifecycle-downgrade), which needs B2 trust material. B1b-3a verifies the file-level `content.hash`; the asset-index and presentation-file hashes are verified in B1b-3b.

CDX-E-DOCUMENT-ID-MISMATCH.summary: The document ID recomputed from the canonical content (Document Hashing section 4) does not equal the declared `manifest.id`.
CDX-E-DOCUMENT-ID-MISMATCH.clause: Document Hashing sections 4.4, 6.3, 7.2; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-DOCUMENT-ID-MISMATCH.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (File `hash` or document-ID mismatch — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-DOCUMENT-ID-MISMATCH.note: STATE-VARYING: WARNING in DRAFT/REVIEW, escalating to INTEGRITY-ERROR on FROZEN/PUBLISHED (state-keyed per Document Hashing section 6.3; deferred to B3 via State Machine section 5.4.2 note 3, as for CDX-E-FILE-HASH-MISMATCH). Recomputed only for a document carrying a real id — a draft's id is `pending` (Document Hashing section 7.1) and has nothing to recompute. A *stale* id (one computed over earlier content or metadata) is exactly what this row detects; a review/frozen/published document carrying a `pending` id is instead a section 7.2 violation this row does not catch, since a pending id is skipped rather than recomputed.

CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING.summary: The Dublin Core metadata part is not available: either the manifest declares no `metadata.dublinCore` reference at all, or the path it declares names no archive entry.
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING.clause: Metadata sections 3.3.1, 3.3.2; Container Format section 3.3.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing required metadata — the Dublin Core part or a required term — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING.note: STATE-VARYING: WARNING in DRAFT/REVIEW, escalating to INTEGRITY-ERROR on FROZEN/PUBLISHED, where the projected Dublin Core terms enter the document ID and the document asserts them fixed. The escalation is deferred to B3 via State Machine section 5.4.2 note 3, which requires a projection-covering signature before `state` can be trusted. AMBIGUITY RECORDED: `metadata.dublinCore` is a REQUIRED manifest field, so the no-reference-at-all case also reads as the section 5.4.2 'Manifest ... missing ... a required field' row, which is REJECT. This vocabulary assigns the more specific missing-metadata row and its narrower WARNING; a future clarification may move that one arm to REJECT. Per State Machine section 5.4.2 note 5, an encrypted part mapped to a stored `.enc` entry satisfies presence and MUST NOT fire this code; that mapping arrives with the security extension's part handling.

CDX-E-METADATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.summary: The Dublin Core metadata part cannot be used as Dublin Core: a syntax error, a resource-limit failure, a valid JSON value that is not an object, or an object the metadata projection REJECTS — a non-object `terms`, a wrong-typed `title`/`description`, or a `creator`/`subject`/`language` that is neither a string nor an array of strings.
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.clause: Metadata section 3; Document Hashing section 4.3.2; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing required metadata — the Dublin Core part or a required term — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-METADATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.note: STATE-VARYING exactly as CDX-E-METADATA-PART-MISSING: WARNING in DRAFT/REVIEW, INTEGRITY-ERROR on FROZEN/PUBLISHED, deferred to B3. An unreadable part is treated as unavailable rather than as empty metadata: the document ID projects the real terms, so recomputing over an empty projection would compare a different document's basis and manufacture a spurious CDX-E-DOCUMENT-ID-MISMATCH. The id is therefore reported as indeterminate, not mismatched. A DUPLICATE KEY in the part is not this code — it is the state-invariant REJECT CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS (State Machine section 5.4.3). The unprojectable-term arm is reported here rather than as a missing term because the projection THROWS on it: the metadata cannot enter the document ID at all, so the id is indeterminate. Left unreported it would silently disable the document-ID check from inside the recompute's error handling, which one malformed ADVISORY term would then be enough to switch off.

CDX-E-METADATA-TERM-MISSING.summary: The Dublin Core part loads but omits a term the specification requires: `title` (a non-empty string) or `creator` (at least one value, in either the scalar or the array form).
CDX-E-METADATA-TERM-MISSING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing required metadata — the Dublin Core part or a required term — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-METADATA-TERM-MISSING.note: STATE-VARYING as for the other two metadata codes: WARNING in DRAFT/REVIEW, INTEGRITY-ERROR on FROZEN/PUBLISHED, deferred to B3. The part still parses, so the document ID remains computable and is verified normally — a missing term lowers metadata quality without making the identity indeterminate. Only `title` and `creator` are required; every other Dublin Core term is optional (Metadata section 3.3).

CDX-E-PART-MISSING-UNBOUND.summary: A manifest reference that carries a path but NO hash names an archive entry that does not exist — the provenance record, a `metadata.jsonld` side file, a collaboration comments or changes file, or the phantom clusters file.
CDX-E-PART-MISSING-UNBOUND.clause: Security Extension section 9.8; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-PART-MISSING-UNBOUND.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing a referenced part outside the document hash and manifest projection — WARNING in every state).
CDX-E-PART-MISSING-UNBOUND.note: STATE-INVARIANT: WARNING in draft, review, frozen and published alike. A path-only reference binds nothing — the target is in neither the document hash nor the manifest projection (extensions overview, Integrity Status of Extension Data) — so its absence degrades a layer and cannot signal tampering. This is deliberately NOT the hash-BOUND missing-part row (a declared presentation layer, an asset index), which escalates to INTEGRITY-ERROR when frozen and is verified in B1b-3b-2. A part that is present but unparseable is CDX-E-EXTENSION-DATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE, not this code. `security.signatures` and `security.encryption` are path-only too but are verified with B2's trust material. Per State Machine section 5.4.2 note 5, an encrypted part mapped to a stored `.enc` entry satisfies presence and MUST NOT fire this code.

CDX-E-EXTENSION-DATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.summary: An out-of-hash extension data part — a collaboration comments or changes file, a phantom clusters file, form data, or the core annotations file — is present but is not well-formed JSON.
CDX-E-EXTENSION-DATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.clause: Extensions overview (Integrity Status of Extension Data, Out-of-hash version skew); State Machine sections 5.4.2, 5.4.3
CDX-E-EXTENSION-DATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Missing or unparseable out-of-hash extension data part — WARNING in every state).
CDX-E-EXTENSION-DATA-PART-UNPARSEABLE.note: STATE-INVARIANT: these bytes sit in no signature scope and in no hash, so a defect in them can never signal tampering — the extensions overview states directly that a missing or unparseable out-of-hash data part is a WARNING in all states and MUST NOT be reported as an INTEGRITY-ERROR. Scoped to the conventional out-of-hash locations (`collaboration/`, `phantoms/`, `forms/`, `security/annotations.json`) plus any path the manifest declares for them; an unrecognized file elsewhere in the archive is IGNORE (State Machine section 5.4.2), never this code. A DUPLICATE KEY in such a part remains the state-invariant REJECT CDX-E-PART-DUPLICATE-KEYS (State Machine section 5.4.3): an unrejected duplicate permits a split-view substitution regardless of which layer carries it.

CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING.summary: A core anchor reference in hashed content resolves to no block or anchor id in the document: a `link` mark whose `href` begins `#` and names an identifier the content does not define.
CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING.clause: Anchors and References sections 7.2, 2.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling core anchor reference in hashed content — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING.note: STATE-VARYING: WARNING in DRAFT/REVIEW, escalating to INTEGRITY-ERROR on FROZEN/PUBLISHED (Anchors and References section 7.2 states this directly — content is fluid below frozen, so a target may not exist yet; above it, a broken anchor indicates corruption). The escalation is deferred to B3 via State Machine section 5.4.2 note 3. A core anchor is part of the document's addressing layer, so a dangling one is an internal-consistency failure of signed content — unlike an extension cross-reference (CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING), which only degrades rendering. A reference that does not begin `#` addresses nothing in this document and is not a defect. Offset and range validity within a resolved target (Anchors and References section 7.3) is a separate check, deferred to B1b-3c.

CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING.summary: A Content Anchor URI carried in an extension BLOCK field resolves to no block or anchor id: `academic:proof` `of`, an `academic:theorem` `uses[]` element, or a `semantic:ref` or `presentation:reference` `target`.
CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING.clause: Anchors and References sections 7.2, 11; Document Hashing section 4.3.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling core anchor reference in hashed content — WARNING in draft/review).
CDX-E-BLOCK-REFERENCE-DANGLING.note: STATE-VARYING as CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING, and deferred to B3 on the same grounds. CLASSIFICATION RECORDED AS CONTESTED, which is why these fields carry their own code rather than sharing CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING. They are treated here as core anchors: Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5 rewrites them into the same relabelled identifier namespace as a `link` mark, and State Machine section 5.4.2's extension-cross-reference carve-out names only MARKS. Against that reading, Anchors and References section 11 groups `semantic:ref` and `presentation:reference` with the cross-reference mechanisms rather than with the core `link` mark, and section 5.4.2's preamble defines a core anchor as a `link` href, an `anchor` mark, or a STRUCTURED Content Anchor (the object form). Draft and review are WARNING under either reading, so the two differ only in the frozen column; separating the codes lets B3 settle that without re-pointing a published code, which the compatibility policy forbids.

CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING.summary: An extension cross-reference mark resolved at render time points at nothing: an `academic:theorem-ref`, `academic:equation-ref`, or `academic:algorithm-ref` whose `target` Content Anchor URI names no defined identifier.
CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING.clause: Anchors and References section 11; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling extension cross-reference resolved at render time — WARNING in every state).
CDX-E-CROSS-REFERENCE-DANGLING.note: STATE-INVARIANT: WARNING in every state, and State Machine section 5.4.2's preamble gives the reason — such a mark is resolved at render time to inject a label, number, or definition, so a dangling one degrades rendering only; the signed bytes remain intact and hash-verified. This is the disposition that distinguishes these marks from the core anchors of CDX-E-ANCHOR-DANGLING, which escalate. COVERAGE IS PARTIAL: the citation, footnote and glossary marks named by the same row are NOT yet resolved. Their targets do not live in the content part — a `citation` mark's `refs` address bibliography entry ids (a `semantic:bibliography` block's `entries`, and/or `semantic/bibliography.json`), and a `glossary` mark's `ref` addresses `semantic/glossary.json`, a file Document Hashing section 4.3.1 deliberately does not relabel. Both side files are `{path, hash}` config references bound by the manifest projection, so they are resolved in B1b-3b-2. The `footnote` mark's `id` is deferred further: the corresponding `semantic:footnote` block matches by `number` or `symbol`, so `id` addresses no clearly specified namespace and the gap is recorded as a specification question rather than guessed at.

CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-DANGLING.summary: An anchor originating in an out-of-hash annotation layer points at content that does not exist: a collaboration comment or change anchor, a change `position` block id, a phantom cluster anchor, or a core annotation anchor naming no defined identifier.
CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-DANGLING.clause: Anchors and References section 7.2; Extensions overview (Integrity Status of Extension Data); State Machine sections 5.4.2, 5.4.3
CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-DANGLING.dispositionClause: State Machine section 5.4.2 (Dangling anchor originating in an out-of-hash annotation layer — WARNING in every state).
CDX-E-ANNOTATION-ANCHOR-DANGLING.note: STATE-INVARIANT: the anchoring layer's bytes are bound by neither the document hash nor the manifest projection, so a dangling anchor cannot signal tampering with signed content, in any state. Resolved only at the anchor positions the extension schemas DECLARE — `annotations[].anchor`, a comment or change `anchor`, a change `position.before`/`.after` block id, and a cluster `anchor`. A generic sweep for any `blockId` or `#` string would be wrong, not merely noisy: a phantom carries a full core content tree whose internal marks address the phantom's own interior, and a collaboration change record carries verbatim before/after block snapshots that legitimately name removed content. State Machine section 5.4.3 forbids escalating a defect confined to an out-of-hash layer's internal graph at all — such a defect is a layer-validity disposition, not an entry in the integrity table.

CDX-E-ID-COLLISION.summary: An identifier is defined more than once in the document's shared identifier namespace — block ids, `anchor` mark ids, equation-line ids and subfigure ids, which together form one namespace requiring uniqueness.
CDX-E-ID-COLLISION.clause: Anchors and References sections 4, 7.2; Document Hashing section 4.3.1; State Machine section 5.4.2
CDX-E-ID-COLLISION.dispositionClause: Anchors and References section 7.2 (ID collides with another ID in the shared namespace — Error in ALL states), whose severities section 7.2 maps onto the WARNING and INTEGRITY-ERROR dispositions of State Machine section 5.4.
CDX-E-ID-COLLISION.note: STATE-INVARIANT, and the only INTEGRITY-ERROR this layer assigns before B2/B3: because the disposition does not vary by state, it needs no projection-covering signature to be sound, unlike every deferred frozen/published escalation. Anchors and References section 7.2 makes a collision an Error in all states — a duplicate makes a reference ambiguous, so which content an anchor addresses is undecidable. The canonicalizer already refuses such a document (Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5 rejects a duplicate id while relabelling), which is why this is reported before the document-ID recompute rather than left to surface as an unexplained inability to compute the id. The namespace is exactly the one Document Hashing section 4.3.1 item 5 relabels, so identifiers addressing SEPARATE namespaces — a bibliography entry's citation key, a footnote or glossary mark id — do not collide with it.
